tool_input.body:
## Summary

GitHub stopped allocating the `macos-14` runner label — jobs cancel in ~1s with no runner assigned (confirmed 2026-11-06; `macos-latest` allocates and passes). PR #240 moved `test.yml`'s CI matrix; this finishes the class across the rest of the repo so a release tag won't fail on the dead runner.

- **`release.yml`** — `smoke-brew` and `bottle` matrices use `macos-latest`. The bottle job already reads its tag dynamically from `*.bottle.json` (not hardcoded) and validates with an `arm64_<codename>` regex, so the tag floating `arm64_sonoma` → `arm64_sequoia` needs no code change — only the explanatory comments.
- **`test.yml`** — stale `macos-14` mentions in comments/step names.
- **`docs/CI.md`** — required-check names now read `build (macos-latest, debug, build)` / `install-brew (macos-latest)`, matching the updated master ruleset.
- **`docs/RELEASING.md`** — bottle-tag section rewritten for the floating codename.
- **`packaging/homebrew/xboing.rb`** — comment reference.

Closes `xboing-xvxi`.

## Test plan

- [x] `macos-latest` allocates runners and passes (proven on #240)
- [x] Both workflow YAMLs parse
- [x] `docs/CI.md` + `docs/RELEASING.md` pass markdownlint
- [x] No `macos-14` left in active files (only historical quarry transcripts, which are excluded)
- [ ] CI green

tool_input.new_string:
from whatever version the `macos-latest` runner currently images,
  not the numeric "15"). The tag floats with `macos-latest`.
  Homebrew bottle compatibility is one-way: a bottle built on a
  given macOS serves that version and *newer* hosts, but an *older*
  host refuses it and falls back to a source build. So building on
  `macos-latest` sets the minimum-supported floor — users on a macOS
  older than the runner's image get no bottle. When GitHub advances
  `macos-latest` to a new OS, the next release's bottle carries the
  new codename and raises that floor. There is no macOS Intel bottle
  in this scope — the tap is Apple Silicon only, matching the
  `macos-latest` (arm64) runner.
